question: Does showing only available memory actions and reusing current notes turn repeated-write failures into independently valid improved proposals?
scope: Four fixed pairs of seeded real-model CPU research workflow diagnostics. Not a test of whether memory beats no memory, nor long-horizon/cross-domain efficacy.
budget_bound: 8 fresh processes, each shares 200000-token envelope across two research invocations, max token price $5/M = $8 total; reserve $16. No fallback. Normal Pro license.

arms.A: Frozen previous memory prompt and instructions; same current research implementation otherwise.
arms.B: State-aware memory prompt, reuse notes, empty refresh example. Same storage/source/budget guards.

model_temperature: existing provider default; remote generation is not seed-controlled
seed_note: Both seeds generated and evaluated by actual native CPU before research. Valid seed value 14; optimal candidate not supplied.
rules: Same prior diagnostic instructions in both arms: save one not-yet-stored counterexample when possible, then improve without repeating notes.
primary: Projects with at least one independently recomputed valid new candidate strictly better than seed value 14.
secondary: complete elapsed seconds including seeds, all failures, memory and candidate evaluation
invalid candidates and repeated invalid schedules
memory revisions, duplicate notes, update-limit/invalid-response failures
actual prompt revisions and source qualification
analysis: Keep all eight planned slots and every failure; separately report seed and new candidate scores, equal-quality pair times, and observed counts. No retry to choose winning samples or retrospective early-stopping savings.
next_gate: Retain simplification if tests preserve write/source guards and real diagnostics show useful proposals without greater protocol failure; report inconclusive or regressions honestly.
